caption: Balaam’s future ruler has a serious messianic history. But “not now” gives no date, and the cited New Testament verses never connect Jesus with this oracle.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Balaam predict Jesus’s timing? Balaam sees a future ruler from Israel and says, “I see him, but not now.” Christians identify that ruler with Jesus.
slides.body: Balaam sees a future ruler from Israel and says, “I see him, but not now.” Christians identify that ruler with Jesus.
slides.heading: Did Balaam predict Jesus’s timing?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Num 24:17: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come forth from Jacob.
slides.body: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come forth from Jacob.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: This is a genuine royal oracle The star and sceptre describe a ruler, and both Jewish and Christian readers have understood the passage as messianic.
slides.body: The star and sceptre describe a ruler, and both Jewish and Christian readers have understood the passage as messianic.
slides.heading: This is a genuine royal oracle

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But “not now” dates nothing The phrase could fit any later ruler. John and Galatians say Jesus came, but never connect him with this oracle.
